data.name: Gentry
data.long_meaning: From the Old English word 'genehten' meaning 'to enter'. The name Gentry can be translated to 'Entrance' or 'Gatekeeper'. In medieval England, the name was given to those who lived near an entrance to a castle or manor.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gentry carries an aristocratic and noble connotation, often associated with the English gentry class, who were the landed nobility of the Middle Ages. Their wealth, power, and status were derived from the ownership of land, making the name synonymous with honors, titles, and prestige.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name Gentry can be seen as a reminder of the entrance to eternal life, which is granted through faith in Jesus Christ. As gatekeepers of the spiritual realm, those with the name Gentry may feel a sense of responsibility to share the message of salvation with others, helping to usher people through the gates of faith and into a deeper relationship with God. Additionally, the name can be seen as a reminder of the importance of being open to the guidance and wisdom God provides, allowing Him to enter and guide our lives as we journey on our spiritual journey.
